currentContext.expansion: The annual report announces no new sugar, cogeneration or distillery capacity project. The Company's installed footprint is unchanged — two sugar factories at Kattur and Sathamangalam, Tamil Nadu, with combined crushing capacity of 6,400 tons of cane per day, 33 MW of power generation and a distillery of 60 KLPD. The binding constraint is cane supply rather than hardware: because of steep reduction in sugarcane availability the Company optimised operations by running the Kattur unit alone and did not operate Sathamangalam in 2025-26, and management states that it may take a couple of years to develop sufficient cane to operate both units at optimum capacity. Consequently the expansion effort is directed at the cane base and at process/technology investment rather than at new lines: incentives for planting approved varieties, latest cultivation technology, mechanisation and water conservation, new high-yield/high-recovery varieties developed with ICAR-SBI and TNAU, and AI-based crop monitoring and technical support, with fresh cane planting in the command area expected to rise around 30% in the current sugar season and overall acreage including ratoon crop up around 30%. On the technology-absorption side, the Company produces six liquid bio-fertilisers at Kattur in technical collaboration with Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, has taken up an AI crop-monitoring pilot across 200 acres, and has deployed about 25 sugarcane harvesters through entrepreneurs to cut harvesting labour cost and dependency. The one standing investment programme disclosed is the Research & Development unit, which commenced operations in April 2023 and focuses on developing value-added products from sugar and by-products with bio-fermentation as a key area; capital outlay in the R&D unit so far is around Rs. 30 Crores. Conservation of Energy for the year is reported as Nil. Existing offtake infrastructure continues unchanged — a long-term PPA with TANGEDCO/TNPDCL for the Sathamangalam unit at a tariff of Rs. 5.189/Kwh, with surplus power from Kattur sold to open access consumers through bilateral agreements and IEX.

risks.risk: Sugarcane availability in the command area — structural raw-material shortage
risks.note: Cane availability for the 2025-26 crushing season was lower by around 10% versus 2024-25, forcing the Company to operate the Kattur unit alone and keep Sathamangalam idle. Management states that high labour cost, better revenue from competitive crops and fear of pest & disease will adversely affect raw material availability and in turn overall capacity utilisation, with a cascading effect during the 2026-27 crushing season.

risks.risk: Pest and disease incidence in sugarcane, and farmer switching to competitive crops
risks.note: Pest and disease in the central part of Tamil Nadu and in the Company's own command area forced farmers to switch to alternative crops as a rotation measure, while paddy, tapioca, banana and gingelly fetch better revenue than sugarcane — directly shrinking the cane base the mills depend on.

risks.risk: Industry oversupply — sugar selling price falling below cost of production
risks.note: Whenever there is surplus sugar production in the country the selling price falls below the cost of production, and because global production is usually surplus at the same time, exports also become unviable, leaving no relief valve for domestic surplus.

risks.risk: Regulated cost-price squeeze — FRP rises while MSP is frozen
risks.note: Sugarcane procurement price has increased year on year (FRP up 4.50%) while the Minimum Selling Price of sugar, fixed at Rs. 31/Kg in February 2019, has not been increased, and the actual selling price is market driven — compressing the sugar segment as lower volumes raise cost of production per ton.

India has an estimated ethanol surplus of nearly 20 billion litres against only around 11 billion litres contracted by oil marketing companies after 20% blending was achieved in March 2025; the gap has led to underuse of distillery capacity and concerns about financial pressure across the sector, threatening the distillery leg that has been the offset to sugar.

risks.risk: Molasses feedstock dependence and tax leakage in the distillery
risks.note: With own molasses inadequate the Company had to procure 58,842 metric tons from other factories in and outside Tamil Nadu at higher prices, and had to absorb GST on bought-out molasses and other input credits as costs following implementation of VAT on Extra Neutral Alcohol — a structural margin leak tied to cane shortfall.

Vagaries in the monsoon pattern affect availability of sugarcane, the major raw material; predictions of a below-normal southwest monsoon in India during 2026 are expected to impact cane planting acreage from current levels, and reduced sales in 2025-26 were partly attributed to scanty rainfall.

risks.risk: Agricultural labour scarcity and rising labour cost in Tamil Nadu
risks.note: Reduction in the availability of agricultural labour and a sharp increase in labour cost have a serious impact on cane cultivation, with most factories unable to get adequate cane supply to their rated crushing capacity; harvesting is the most labour-intensive and expensive activity, making mechanisation urgent.

risks.risk: Operating leverage — under-utilisation of fixed assets across all three segments
risks.note: Lower crushing cascades through the whole complex: sugar production down around 9%, alcohol production down and power generation lower, with export of power to the grid declining by over 72% as crushing ran under capacity more frequently due to erratic sugarcane supplies.

one_liner.body: Kothari Sugars and Chemicals Limited is a Tamil Nadu-based integrated sugar manufacturer operating two sugar factories with co-generated power and a distillery at Kattur and Sathamangalam.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: KSCL manufactures sugar, alcohol and power from sugarcane at its units at Kattur and Sathamangalam in Tamil Nadu. The Company operates in three major segments — Sugar, Cogeneration of power (Cogen) and Distillery — with cane sourced from farmers in its command area, supplemented by molasses bought from other factories within and outside Tamil Nadu for the distillery. Power is sold to the state utility under a long-term PPA from the Sathamangalam unit and to open access consumers and IEX from the Kattur unit, while alcohol/ethanol is supplied to Oil Marketing Companies.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Sugar:** Sugar (from cane crushing)
- **Distillery:** Alcohol, Ethanol supplied to Oil Marketing Companies, Extra Neutral Alcohol
- **Power:** Co-generated power sold under long-term PPA and to open access consumers / IEX
- **By-products:** Bagasse, Molasses
- **Bio-fertilisers (Kattur, in technical collaboration with TNAU):** Glucono Acetobacter Diazotrophicus - Nitrogen Fixer, Phospho Bacteria - Bacillus magaterium (PSB) - Phosphorus Solubilizer, Phospho Bacteria - Arbuscular mycorrhizae (AM fungi) - Phosphorus Mobilizer, Frareuria Aurantia - Paenibacillus Mucilaginosus - Potash Release Bacteria, Zinc Solubilizer - Pseudomonas Chloroaphis (ZSB), Vasicular Arbuscular Mycorrhize (VAM)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:

- TNPDCL / TANGEDCO under a long-term PPA for the Sathamangalam unit
- Open access consumers and IEX (power exchange) for surplus power from the Kattur unit
- Tamil Nadu sugarcane command area farmers (cane development, bio-fertilisers)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's sugar production for SS 2025-26 estimated at around 29.3 million metric tons after diversion of juice/syrup/B-Heavy molasses, leaving closing stock of around 2.5 months of sugar availability — hence sugar price is likely to be stable
- Global sugar production expected around 186.7 million metric tons against consumption of around 178.50 million metric tons, a surplus of 8.3 million metric tons; 2026-27 SS is also expected to be a marginally surplus year
- Predictions of a below-normal southwest monsoon in India during 2026 expected to impact cane planting acreage from current levels
- Central Government push for ethanol — subsidies for new ethanol plants and higher procurement prices for B-Heavy molasses ethanol — absorbing a significant portion of surplus sugar production and, in the long run, letting India balance sugar and ethanol output to market requirements
- Government policies such as MSP and the monthly sugar release mechanism expected to help stabilise sugar price
- Ethanol overcapacity and market glut — an estimated surplus of nearly 20 billion litres against only around 11 billion litres contracted by oil marketing companies, leading to underuse of distillery capacity and financial pressure across the sector; India achieved 20% ethanol blending in March 2025
- Policymakers and industry exploring new ethanol uses beyond cars and two-wheelers — ethanol cooking stoves, ethanol-diesel blending for generators and flex-fuel vehicles
- Sugarcane procurement price (FRP) has risen year on year while the MSP of sugar, fixed at Rs. 31/Kg in February 2019, has not been increased; actual selling price remains market driven
- Reduced availability of agricultural labour in Tamil Nadu and sharp increase in labour cost seriously impact cane cultivation, with most factories unable to get adequate cane supply to rated crushing capacity — making mechanisation of cane cultivation urgent
- Vagaries in the monsoon pattern and continued pest and disease incidence in the central and coastal zones of Tamil Nadu to impact availability of sugarcane, the major raw material
- Company-specific: cane availability for the 2025-26 crushing season was lower by around 10% versus 2024-25 while sugar recovery was around 3% higher; pest and disease and better-paying competitive crops (paddy, tapioca, banana, gingelly) pushed farmers to alternative crops
- Distillery economics pressured by molasses shortage requiring out-of-state purchases at higher prices, and by absorption of GST on bought-out molasses and other input credits as cost following implementation of VAT on Extra Neutral Alcohol

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Give top priority to sugarcane development in the command area by optimising utilisation of all resources, to restore cane availability and capacity utilisation
- Improve sugarcane yield through an AI platform
- Develop new sugarcane clones with higher yield, high sugar recovery, early maturity, drought tolerance and pest & disease resistance in association with SISMA, TNAU and the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore
- Bulk planting of high-yield, high-sugar varieties such as Co-86032 and Co-18009 in both units' command areas
- Educate farmers on modern cultivation practices through technical seminars, technical support and demonstration in Demo plots
- Provide technical and financial support to farmers for irrigation infrastructure — well deepening, lift irrigation, new bore/pumps
- Promote water conservation systems such as micro irrigation in association with the State Agriculture Department
- Mechanise cane cultivation from ploughing to harvest to reduce farmers' cultivation cost and dependency on labour
- Optimise crushing operations by running only the viable unit — Kattur was operated alone in 2025-26 and Sathamangalam was not operated, based on viability
- Operate the distillery for the maximum possible number of days by procuring molasses from other factories within and outside Tamil Nadu when own molasses is inadequate
- Water conservation — promoting micro irrigation systems in association with the State Agriculture Department, and providing technical and financial support to farmers for irrigation infrastructure such as well deepening, lift irrigation and installation of new bores/pumps
- Production of six liquid bio-fertilisers at Kattur in technical collaboration with Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (nitrogen fixer, phosphorus solubilizer and mobilizer, potash release bacteria, zinc solubilizer and VAM) to support soil health in the command area
- AI-based crop monitoring pilot across 200 acres to fine tune irrigation frequency and macro/micro nutrient application and improve soil fertility and yield
- Development of new sugarcane clones with drought tolerance and pest & disease resistance in association with SISMA, TNAU and the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore, and bulk planting of high-yield varieties such as Co-86032 and Co-18009
- Farmer capability building — technical seminars, technical support and demonstration plots on modern cultivation practices, plus incentives for planting approved varieties
- Mechanisation of cane cultivation from ploughing to harvest, including about 25 sugarcane harvesters deployed through entrepreneurs, to reduce farmers' cultivation cost and dependency on labour
- Conservation of Energy for the year is reported as Nil

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated sugar-cogeneration-distillery complex allowing the Company to balance sugar, power and alcohol output from the same cane stream
- Long-term PPA with TNPDCL/TANGEDCO for the Sathamangalam unit at a fixed tariff of Rs. 5.189/Kw-hr, with the Kattur unit selling surplus power to open access consumers and IEX
- Distillery flexibility — the Company procured 58,842 metric tons of molasses from other factories within and outside Tamil Nadu to keep the distillery operating for the maximum possible number of days despite inadequate own molasses

- Regulated cost-price squeeze — FRP rises while MSP is frozen — Sugarcane procurement price has increased year on year (FRP up 4.50%) while the Minimum Selling Price of sugar, fixed at Rs. 31/Kg in February 2019, has not been increased, and the actual selling price is market driven — compressing the sugar segment as lower volumes raise cost of production per ton.
- Ethanol overcapacity and market glut — India has an estimated ethanol surplus of nearly 20 billion litres against only around 11 billion litres contracted by oil marketing companies after 20% blending was achieved in March 2025; the gap has led to underuse of distillery capacity and concerns about financial pressure across the sector, threatening the distillery leg that has been the offset to sugar.
- Molasses feedstock dependence and tax leakage in the distillery — With own molasses inadequate the Company had to procure 58,842 metric tons from other factories in and outside Tamil Nadu at higher prices, and had to absorb GST on bought-out molasses and other input credits as costs following implementation of VAT on Extra Neutral Alcohol — a structural margin leak tied to cane shortfall.
- Weather and monsoon dependence — Vagaries in the monsoon pattern affect availability of sugarcane, the major raw material; predictions of a below-normal southwest monsoon in India during 2026 are expected to impact cane planting acreage from current levels, and reduced sales in 2025-26 were partly attributed to scanty rainfall.
- Agricultural labour scarcity and rising labour cost in Tamil Nadu — Reduction in the availability of agricultural labour and a sharp increase in labour cost have a serious impact on cane cultivation, with most factories unable to get adequate cane supply to their rated crushing capacity; harvesting is the most labour-intensive and expensive activity, making mechanisation urgent.
- Operating leverage — under-utilisation of fixed assets across all three segments — Lower crushing cascades through the whole complex: sugar production down around 9%, alcohol production down and power generation lower, with export of power to the grid declining by over 72% as crushing ran under capacity more frequently due to erratic sugarcane supplies.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Give top priority to sugarcane development in the command area by optimising utilisation of all resources, to restore cane availability and capacity utilisation
- Improve sugarcane yield through an AI platform
- Develop new sugarcane clones with higher yield, high sugar recovery, early maturity, drought tolerance and pest & disease resistance in association with SISMA, TNAU and the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore
- Bulk planting of high-yield, high-sugar varieties such as Co-86032 and Co-18009 in both units' command areas
